en.note: Internship project, Aug–Oct 2023. The source is an anonymized display-ad sample — an ad table, an impression log and a user table with coded attribute levels — covering nine days; every number on this page is computed from it at build time.

fig1.title: The metric map: what an e-commerce analyst should measure
fig1.sub: five questions · 52 metrics and models, as written up for the team
fig1.caption: Exhibit 1. The map was the first deliverable: a shared vocabulary from traffic (UV, PV, new users) through demand, the funnel and retention to user value. The RFM tiers in the last column are the ones the segmentation below is labelled with.

fig2.title: The analysis, step by step
fig2.caption: Exhibit 2. The analysis as it was run, in pandas: three tables joined on user and ad, cleaned, banded by price, then read two ways — what gets clicked at each price, and who is looking — before the clicking users were clustered and labelled with the RFM tiers from the map.

fig3.title: Click rate by price band
fig3.sub: 9 price bands · dots = click rate · bars = share of impressions · 975,441 joined impressions
fig3.caption: Exhibit 3. Four in ten impressions were ads under 100, and they were clicked most: 5.5% against 4.2% in the 1,600–6,400 bands. Click rate falls with price until the top band, where it recovers to 5.1% on a base of only 6,236 impressions. Cheap goods carry the traffic; high-ticket ads earn their clicks from a far smaller audience.

fig4.title: Who is looking at each price band
fig4.sub: share of impressions by the viewer's consumption level · users without a level excluded
fig4.caption: Exhibit 4. The audience shifts with price even though click rate barely does. Low-consumption users see 39% of the under-100 impressions and 17% of the 6,400–12,800 band; high-consumption users go from 6% to 20%. Age and shopping depth hardly move across bands, which is why consumption level became the targeting dimension in the recommendations.

fig5.title: Five segments of clicking users, labelled with the RFM tiers
fig5.sub: K-means on shopping depth, click rate and the price of what was clicked · 40,997 users with at least one click · re-run at build time with a fixed seed
fig5.caption: Exhibit 5. Tiers follow the report's rule: click rate stands in for frequency, the price of clicked ads for monetary value. The largest group, 37%, clicks high-priced ads rarely — the win-back tier the recommendations aimed retargeting at. The two groups near a 99% click rate are mostly users seen once, which is the weakness of a nine-day log, not a loyal core.

fig3.title: 各价格区间的点击率与曝光占比
fig3.sub: 9 个价格区间 · 圆点表示点击率，柱形表示曝光占比 · 共 975,441 次已关联曝光
fig3.caption: 图 3：约四成曝光来自价格低于 100 的商品，该区间点击率最高，为 5.5%。随着价格升高，点击率在 1,600—6,400 区间降至约 4.2%，到最高区间回升至 5.1%，但该区间仅有 6,236 次曝光。比较点击率时，需要同时关注各区间的样本规模。

fig4.title: 各价格区间接触到的用户构成
fig4.sub: 按用户消费层级划分的曝光占比，不含消费层级缺失的记录
fig4.caption: 图 4：不同价格区间的点击率差异有限，人群构成却有明显变化。低消费层级用户贡献的曝光占比，从低于 100 区间的 39% 降至 6,400—12,800 区间的 17%；高消费层级则从 6% 升至 20%。年龄和购物层级的构成相对稳定，因此建议将消费层级作为广告投放的人群划分依据。

fig5.title: 有点击行为用户的五类分群
fig5.sub: 对 40,997 名用户进行 K-means 聚类，特征为购物层级、点击率及点击广告的价格；本页采用固定随机种子复算
fig5.caption: 图 5：沿用原报告的命名方式，以点击率和点击广告的价格分别作为频次、金额的替代指标。最大群体占约 37%，点击率相对较低、点击广告价格较高，被命名为「重要挽留用户」，建议通过再营销触达。两个点击率接近 99% 的群体大多仅有一次曝光，不能据此认定其忠诚度高。
